en.title: Longest Common Prefix Across Two Integer Arrays
en.description:
Choose one positive integer from each of the two arrays and compare the common prefix of their usual decimal representations; return the maximum prefix length over all cross-array pairs, or 0 if no pair shares a first digit.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and editorial; supplements to missing source bounds and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n m, the second line contains n numbers, and the third line contains m numbers. Original bounds: 1≤n,m≤50000, 1≤value≤100000000; the largest value has 9 digits.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 3; 0; 9. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Repeatedly divide each number in the first array by 10 to get all its non-empty prefixes and put them in a set; then enumerate the prefixes of the other array to find the longest match.
